Aurum · Visual engineering report · 23 October 2026

More depth from the same small machine

Version 0.5.6 brings the cloud layer into water reflections, deepens leaf shade, softens the washed sunset, and makes generated Pixel 3D relief available on a fresh LOW preset. These are actual Minecraft captures; Photon and Complementary are credited style references.

Branch: codexMinecraft 1.20.1 · FabricLOW preset visual smoke test854 × 480 · Mesa llvmpipe

01 / Result

What changed in the image

Sky and sunset

The sun-facing sky LUT receives less gain at golden hour, and the sun glow is narrower. The LUT now blends across rebuilds instead of snapping between sky colours.

Water and foliage

Water reprojects the previous cloud image into the reflected direction, using the cloud pass already rendered. Leaf interiors receive stronger ambient occlusion while exposed leaves keep their light.

Sharp voxel relief

Fresh LOW enables generated parallax within 16 blocks. Relief is culled when texture pixels are too small on screen; generated heights get softer walls and shadows than authored PBR height maps.

Performance intent: cloud colour uses one existing cloud texture sample at water pixels, with no second cloud ray march. Relief stops when it cannot resolve on screen. These are design choices; this environment cannot establish Intel UHD frame time.
02 / In-game evidence

Same world, camera and time

The paired captures use the same world and viewpoint at clear noon and sunset. The cloud field drifts between runs, so compare scene behaviour and colour, not identical cloud silhouettes. Both runs are 854 × 480 software-rendered tests.

03 / Detail check

Raised pixels, with a necessary restraint

Why the generated map is gentler

A first close pass made gravel look striped. The generated height range, wall normals and self-shadow were softened after this inspection. Height inferred from colour is only an approximation of physical shape; it should add depth without overwhelming the source texture.

The test pack has 0 authored PBR maps among 1,577 block textures. This capture checks generated relief only. Authored LabPBR depth still needs a separate target-hardware scene.

04 / Visual references

The target language

Official gallery images below are references for atmospheric depth, cohesive water colour and a readable game palette. They are not matched-scene benchmarks or Aurum output.

05 / Validation and remaining gaps

What this release proves

BuildGradle build passes; remapped Fabric JAR produced.Packaging and Java compilation pass; repository has no unit tests.
ShadersGLSL expansion and terrain validation pass; 14 Aurum programs compile in Minecraft.OpenGL 3.3 software smoke test passes.
Visual sceneNoon, sunset and close generated-relief scenes inspected.Confirms the captures and catches obvious shader artefacts at 854 × 480.
Intel UHD 620Target GPU unavailable here.1080p image quality, motion stability and frame time require UHD measurements.
Reference parityNot claimed.Vanilla-compatible RGBA8 rendering still tone-maps sky, terrain and water separately; Photon’s full atmosphere and HDR lighting remain larger architectural work.
Known boundary: the cloud reflection reuses the previous onscreen cloud view. Clouds outside that view fall back to the sky LUT, and quick camera moves may reveal the transition. LOW leaves terrain screen-space reflections off by default to protect frame time; the cloud reflection remains available.
